lines.known_text: No, but in terms of informing people that a report was about to be published, you would expect that somebody who's named would at least have an opportunity, 24 hours or a few hours, just to prepare themselves that something was being published that talks about them.

lines.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
lines.target_text: Hynny yw, dwi jest yn derbyn eich bod chi'n rhyw ddi-hid ac yn galon-galed iawn yn hynny o beth.
lines.known_text: I'm just getting that you're being somewhat rash and very hard-hearted in that regard.

lines.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
lines.target_text: Dwi ddim yn sôn am rannu copi o'r adroddiad na dim byd, ond ar lefel cyfrifoldeb moesol i unigolion, dŷch chi ddim yn teimlo unrhyw fath o gyfrifoldeb yn hynny o beth?
lines.known_text: I'm not talking about sharing a copy of the report, but in terms of a moral responsibility to individuals, don't you feel any sort of responsibility in that regard?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Dwi'n teimlo'r cyfrifoldeb moesol tuag at y staff.
lines.known_text: I feel a moral responsibility towards the staff.

lines.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
lines.target_text: Felly, unwaith mae rhywun yn gadael S4C, dyna fe wedyn, ie?
lines.known_text: So, once somebody leaves S4C, that's it, is it?

lines.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
lines.target_text: Os ydyn nhw'n gyn-staff, chi ddim yn rhan o—?
lines.known_text: If they're former staff, you're not part of—?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Na, ni'n sôn fan hyn am bobl, am ddau unigolyn oedd wedi cael eu diswyddo, ac a oedd, fel dwi'n ei ddweud, yn cynnal ymgyrch cyhoeddus iawn, gan ddefnyddio—
lines.known_text: No, we're talking here about people, about two individuals who had been dismissed, and, as I've said, were waging a very public campaign, using—

lines.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
lines.target_text: Wel, os ŷch chi eisiau ei fframio fe mewn modd o un garfan yn erbyn y llall, ond ŷch chi'n ddigon siarp i wybod byddai efallai peidio hysbysu rhywun o flaen llaw yn rhoi arf iddyn nhw ei dwlu yn ôl atoch chi, os dyna'r gêm ŷch chi'n ei chwarae.
lines.known_text: Well, if you want to frame it as one group against another, but you're sharp enough to know that perhaps not informing somebody beforehand would give them something to throw back at you, if that's the game you're playing.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Wel, fe allaf i weld hynny, ond yn y trafodaethau rhyngom ni a'n tîm cyfreithiol, penderfynwyd peidio.
lines.known_text: Well, I can understand that point, but in the discussions between ourselves and our legal team, the decision was taken not to do that.

lines.speaker: Llyr Gruffydd
lines.target_text: Diolch.
lines.known_text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Iawn.
lines.known_text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Fe wnawn ni fynd at Alun.
lines.known_text: We'll go on to Alun Davies now.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: Can I talk to you, Chris?

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: You're one of the most experienced and respected non-executives I've come across in my time, and I'm interested in the answers you gave to earlier questions about the non-execs not understanding and not appreciating the place and the role and what was happening, and you said in answer to an earlier question that there were lessons to be learned.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: I was just hoping that you could outline what some of those lessons were and why you think the organisation has found itself in this position.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: Well, I think—.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: A couple of things to say: I think this was an extremely difficult situation, genuinely.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: It's probably one of the most difficult and unpleasant situations I've had to deal with through a very long career in business.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: And I, you know, am very aware of the impact that has had on individuals, has had on the community of people and the community of stakeholders and so on, so this was a tough situation to deal with.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: I think in terms of the lessons to learn from this, I think we really do need to look at how processes and procedures, which work well in other sectors, in other places and so on, why they perhaps did not work here so well.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: Are there particular cultural reasons for that?

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: Are there particular—?

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: I think in the recent BECTU letter to the committee, that makes reference to the fact that it is a sector with extreme power imbalances, and that is, I think, something that has been looked at by this committee and so on elsewhere.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, that is why I think—

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: But that's not new, is it, and it's not unique to S4C?

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: It isn't, but this has brought into sharp relief the fact that that could create or may have contributed to this extremely difficult and distressing situation for so many people, both individuals and collectively.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, that's why I personally feel, obviously, a sense of responsibility—a huge sense of responsibility—for the way that the company, for what has happened in the company over the last year, which is not what any of us would have wanted, and I will give whatever input and support I can to try to look forward, understanding why, given the particular nature of the company, and the sector and so on, that it works in, and how we can best ensure that doesn't happen again.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: And I think the way to do that is by involving as many different perspectives as possible in that process, as well as looking at good practice from outside, and getting expert input into that.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: But to come back to your question, for me, it is very difficult to say, because a lot was in place that you would have hoped would have prevented this from happening, but it didn't prevent it from happening, and that's the lesson we've got to learn.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: Can I pursue that, please?

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: I want to ask some questions that are quite difficult.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: You had a responsibility for managing the relationship between the chair and the chief executive, and that was, I thought, well aired yesterday in the select committee meeting.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: And one of the issues we found in the Capital Law report, of course, was an issue between the chair and I think it was the chief content officer, wasn't it, where a complaint was upheld against the chair.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: Did non-executive directors, at any time, discuss confidence in the chair, the role—the continuing role—of the chair, in terms of the happenings that were going on at this time?

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: The particular issue you're referring to there was that a particular grievance was raised—

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: —under the S4C grievance policy concerning the chair.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: That was on 16 June, and it referred to a specific event at a meeting that had happened the previous day.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, that grievance wasn't raised with the non-executive directors; it was raised under the policy with the head of HR, who shared that with the company secretary, and they put in place, with appropriate advice from outside, a procedure to hear that grievance on its own merits, and as a specific occurrence.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: And that was in line with the principles of the internal grievance policy.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, that required two independent people to hear the grievance, one of whom was actually a non-exec director, but one who hadn't been involved in the events the previous day, and therefore was completely separate from that, and one was an experienced external HR professional, who was brought in to provide a further independent view of that.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: They heard the grievance from both parties.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: It was a confidential process.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: They then reached their conclusion and shared that conclusion with the parties, and there is a confidential report that summarises their findings.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: Now, because that's a confidential process, the non-executives were not involved in that, but my understanding is that their finding was that, yes, the behaviour of the chair the previous day had been inappropriate on that occasion, it shouldn't have happened, and that a sincere apology should be made, but that that was the appropriate outcome for that specific incident.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: And that is, as I understand it, what happened.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, at that point, that dealt with that grievance under what appeared to be a sensible and appropriate policy.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, there wasn't really a question at that stage of, 'Well, does that mean we don't have confidence in the chair?'—

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: Yes, that's fair enough.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: —but it is fair to say that when the Capital Law report was received, which was in, I think, early November, no, early October—apologies—no, early November; I'm confused.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: At that stage, given various things that were raised in the Capital Law report concerning the chair, it was appropriate for the non-executive directors to meet independently, and to review what had been raised in the Capital Law report, and also any other issues concerning the chair, and take a view as to whether we did have confidence in the chair to continue in that role, to deal with what should be the steps following from the Capital Law report, and what we should do as a board as a consequence.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, that was a meeting of the non-executive directors not involving the chair; it was advised by suitable independent external legal advice, and we reviewed the issues that had been raised in the Capital Law report concerning the chair, and also including the particular grievance that you've referred to.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: We also looked at other issues during the process where—.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: I think it is worth saying that, in a board of directors, what you want is a diversity of view and you want challenge and you want robust debate.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: Of course you do.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, during this whole process, there have been issues in which non-executive directors have challenged decisions that might have been, or suggestions made by the chair; we have debated those, and that is absolutely what you want a board to do.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, we had a full discussion of those issues and decided that, actually, there wasn't anything in the issues raised in the Capital Law report concerning the chair that made it inappropriate for the chair to carry on overseeing, leading, the next stage of the response to the Capital Law report.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, that was a decision that we took collectively as non-executive directors, but did put in place particular mechanisms that would have enabled any point that raised concern—for the chair to have been recused at that point, and for that to have been debated.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, I think we did handle what, again, was a very difficult situation in a sensible way.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: I'm grateful to you for your candour there; that's very useful for the committee.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: Did you—?

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: One of the shocking things that I heard yesterday at the select committee was Rhodri's comment, or answer to a question, that he hadn't met with the Secretary of State in four years.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: I find it extraordinary that a Secretary of State has not met a chair of a national broadcaster in four years.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Wel, gaf i ddweud un gair pellach ynglŷn â hwnna?
lines.known_text: If I could just say one other thing on that issue.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Pan gododd—.
lines.known_text: When—.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Rŷn ni wedi trafod y materion hyn gyda swyddogion DCMS ers derbyn llythyr cyntaf BECTU—gwnes i eu gwneud nhw'n ymwybodol o hynny, ac rŷn ni'n siarad yn gyson.
lines.known_text: We have discussed these issues with DCMS officials since the receipt of the first BECTU letter, and made them aware of that, and we do speak regularly.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Ie, yn amlwg.
lines.known_text: Yes, clearly.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ar fwy nag un achlysur yn ystod y cyfnod yma, dwi wedi gofyn i'r swyddog rŷn ni'n delio gyda fe a fyddai fe'n fuddiol i drefnu cyfarfod wyneb yn wyneb, neu yn rhithiol os ydy e'n dod i hynny, gyda'r Ysgrifennydd Gwladol, a'r ateb a gefais oedd nad oedd angen gwneud hynny, felly.
lines.known_text: On more than one occasion during this period, I have asked the official that we deal with whether it would be beneficial to arrange a face-to-face meeting, or a virtual meeting if it came to that, with the Secretary of State, and the response I was given was that that was not necessary.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Dwi'n ffeindio hynny'n hollol shocking—shocking.
lines.known_text: I find that completely shocking—shocking.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: I rywun sydd actually yn credu dylai darlledu ddim cael ei ddatganoli, dyw hynny ddim yn rhywbeth buaswn i wedi eisiau ei glywed.
lines.known_text: For someone who actually thinks that broadcasting shouldn't be devolved, that isn't something I would have wanted to hear.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Mae'n adlewyrchu problemau mawr gan y DCMS, dwi'n meddwl.
lines.known_text: It reflects great problems with the DCMS, I think.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Ond roeddwn i'n mynd i ofyn cwestiwn arall i Chris, os caf i.
lines.known_text: But I was going to ask another question to Chris, if I may.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Yn ystod y trafodaethau dŷch chi wedi bod yn eu cael fel bwrdd ac fel non-execs yn ystod y cyfnod yma, a wnaethoch chi ofyn am gymorth neu gefnogaeth gan y DCMS, gan y BBC, neu gan Lywodraeth Cymru, o unrhyw un o'r cyrff llywodraethol, fel petai?
lines.known_text: During the discussions that you've been having as a board and as non-execs during this period, did you ask for support from the DCMS, the BBC, or Welsh Government, from any one of those governmental organisations?

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: Did we—

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.known_text: Did you seek support or advice as non-execs?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Efallai ei fod e'n haws i fi ateb hwnna, ydy e, Chris?
lines.known_text: Perhaps it would be easier for me to answer that, Chris.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: Well, I will think whilst you answer.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Hynny yw, fe drafodon ni gyda'r DCMS a gyda Llywodraeth Cymru i sicrhau eu bod nhw'n ymwybodol o'r materion proses, a liciwn i bwysleisio hynny: doedd yna ddim cwestiwn o rannu gyda nhw unrhyw ganfyddiadau neu beth fyddai'n dod allan o'r adroddiad, a fyddai hynny ddim wedi bod yn bosibl achos doeddem ni ddim yn gwybod tan fod y tîm o fewn Capital Law yn cyflwyno eu hadroddiad nhw i ni.
lines.known_text: Well, we did have discussions with the DCMS and Welsh Government to ensure that they were aware of the procedural issues, and I'd like to emphasise that: there was no question of sharing any findings or the results of the report, and that wouldn't have been possible because we didn't know until the team within Capital Law presented their report to us.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ac, ar bob achlysur, yr ymateb—ac yn fwy pendant gan DCMS na gan neb arall—yr ateb oedd mai mater gweithredol i fwrdd S4C oedd hwn, ac nad eu lle nhw oedd cynghori.
lines.known_text: And, on all occasions, the response—and more specifically from DCMS than anywhere else—was that this was an operational issue for the S4C board, and it wasn't their place to advise.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Ie, ie.
lines.known_text: Yes, yes.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Ond cwestiwn jest tipyn yn wahanol gyda phwyslais gwahanol oedd gen i i Chris: a oeddech chi wedi gofyn am gefnogaeth tra roeddech chi'n ystyried—achos dwi'n cymryd, fel non-execs, roeddech chi'n trafod ymhlith eich gilydd beth oedd yn digwydd, ac roedd yna adroddiadau yn y cyfryngau; mi fuasai fe'n od petaech chi ddim yn siarad gyda'ch gilydd—wedi gofyn am gefnogaeth allanol i'ch helpu chi ddelio gyda'r peth, y materion yma?
lines.known_text: But I had a slightly different question, with a different emphasis, to Chris: had you asked for support while you were considering—because I take it, as non-execs, you were discussing amongst yourselves what was happening, and there were reports in the media; it would have been odd if you weren't talking to each other—had you asked for external support to help you deal with these issues?

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: I think the most helpful thing I can say is that, yes, as a group of non-executive directors including the chair, company secretary, in terms of processes to follow et cetera, yes, as Rhodri's explained, for example, DCMS would have been in the loop on that.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: For us as a group of non-executive directors excluding the chair, then we looked to expert advice from our legal advisers on those points, and that was provided.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, for example, in response to the issues raised in the Capital Law report, we had specific legal advice on those issues of conflict, and that was very helpful to us.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: But I don't remember any other circumstance in which the non-execs on their own—.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: I certainly don't remember where they needed to look to other wider bodies for input.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Ocê.
lines.known_text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Diolch am hynny.
lines.known_text: Thank you for that.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Rhodri, os caf fi jest bennu gyda hwn: mi fuasech chi wedi gweld adroddiadau gan y pwyllgor dethol ar ôl eich ymddangosiad ddoe.
lines.known_text: Rhodri, if I could just end on this: you will have seen reports from the select committee after your appearance yesterday.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Maen nhw wedi dweud bod angen arweinyddiaeth newydd ar S4C.
lines.known_text: They have said there's a need for new leadership at S4C.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Pan ofynnodd, dwi'n credu, Steve Crabb, ichi os oeddech chi'n mynd i wneud cais am eich ailbenodi ym mis Ebrill, roeddech chi wedi rhoi ateb braidd yn od, i fy nghlustiau i, eich bod chi'n fodlon derbyn eich ailbenodi.
lines.known_text: When, I think, Steve Crabb, asked you whether you were going to seek reappointment in April, you gave quite an odd answer, in my opinion, that you would be happy to accept reappointment.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Doeddech chi ddim yn dweud eich bod chi'n mynd i wneud cais am hynny; roeddech chi'n dweud eich bod chi'n derbyn eich ailbenodi.
lines.known_text: You didn't say that you were going to apply for that; you said that you would be happy to accept a reappointment.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Roeddwn i'n clywed hynny braidd yn od, y ffordd o eirio pethau.
lines.known_text: I thought that was an odd way of wording things.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Ond ydych chi wedi ystyried, dros nos, eich sefyllfa a ble dŷch chi'n sefyll heddiw ar ôl clywed barn y pwyllgor dethol?
lines.known_text: Have you considered, overnight, your position and where you stand today after hearing the views of the select committee?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ydw, wrth gwrs dwi wedi, ac wedi trafod gydag eraill yr hyn ddigwyddodd ddoe.
lines.known_text: Yes, of course, and I have discussed with others what happened yesterday.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Yr hyn oedd yn fy synnu i ynglŷn â'n trafodaeth ni ddoe doedd ddim yr elfen dyw'r pwyllgor ddim yn awyddus i fi gael fy ailbenodi, ond y pwyslais i gyd ynglŷn â materion proses ac ynglŷn â diwedd y broses yma.
lines.known_text: What surprised me in our discussion yesterday wasn't this element that the committee wasn't eager to see me reappointed, but the emphasis being solely on process and the end of this process.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Doedd yna ddim ffocws o gwbl ddoe ar yr hyn mae aelodau staff S4C wedi'i ddioddef.
lines.known_text: There was no focus whatsoever yesterday on what staff members in S4C have suffered.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Doedd yna ddim unrhyw bryder yn cael ei fynegi ynglŷn â'r hyn maen nhw wedi gorfod ei ddioddef dros gyfnod hir o fisoedd.
lines.known_text: There was no concern expressed about what they have had to go through over a long period of months.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Fy mhryder i yw bod peth o—.
lines.known_text: My concern is that—.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae llawer o bobl wedi gwneud sylwadau ynglŷn â beth ddylai ddigwydd.
lines.known_text: Many people have commented on what should happen.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Dwi ddim yn amau eu cymhelliad nhw o gwbl, ond dyw unrhyw beth sydd yn creu ansefydlogrwydd pellach i'n staff ni ddim yn help i'r staff a dyw e ddim yn help i'r sefydliad yn ei gyfanrwydd.
lines.known_text: I don't doubt their motivation at all, but anything that creates further instability for our staff is not going to help the staff and it's not going to help the organisation as a whole either.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: A dyna pam, pe bai'r Ysgrifennydd Gwladol yn gofyn—.
lines.known_text: That's why, if the Secretary of State were to ask me—.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: A dyna'r broses—hynny yw, does dim cwestiwn o wneud cais.
lines.known_text: And that is the process—there's no question of making an application.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Does dim proses ymgeisio; mater i'r Ysgrifennydd Gwladol yw ailbenodi cadeirydd neu aelodau cyrff, ac mae e'n glir iawn hefyd yn y rheolau.
lines.known_text: There is no application process, as such; it's a matter for the Secretary of State to reappoint a chair or members of bodies, and it is very clear too in the rules and regulations.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ac fel roeddet ti'n ddigon caredig i gyfeirio ato'n gynt, dwi wedi bod o gwmpas digon hir i wybod na ddylid cymryd yn ganiataol byth, y bydd yna ailbenodiad yn digwydd, a dyna pam roeddwn i wedi defnyddio'r ffurf o eiriau fe wnes i.
lines.known_text: And as you kindly referred to earlier, I've been around long enough to know that one should never take it for granted that there will be a reappointment, and that's why I had used the wording that I did.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Dwi'n deall hynny.
lines.known_text: I understand that.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Rhodri, gest ti dy arestio yn ymgyrchu dros S4C, do?
lines.known_text: Rhodri, you were arrested in campaigning for S4C, weren't you?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Sawl gwaith.
lines.known_text: A number of times.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Sawl gwaith; dwi'n cofio.
lines.known_text: A number of times.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Ac mae dy ymrwymiad di i S4C wedi bod trwy dy fywyd di.
lines.known_text: Your commitment to S4C has been lifelong.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Dwi'n deall hynny a dwi ddim yn cwestiynu hynny o gwbl.
lines.known_text: I understand that and I don't question that.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Mae'r issues dŷn ni wedi'u gweld dros y blynyddoedd diwethaf wedi bod yn anodd iawn, a dwi'n deall hynny.
lines.known_text: But the issues we've seen over the last few years have been very difficult, and I understand that.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Ond yr hyn sydd gen i yw, pan ŷch chi'n sôn am ddioddefaint aelodau staff S4C, ti oedd yn rhan o'r arweinyddiaeth wnaeth achosi hynny, ac mae'n rhaid, wedi hynny—.
lines.known_text: But what I'm saying is, when you're talking about the suffering of staff members at S4C, you were part of the leadership that caused that.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Roeddech chi'n dweud yn gynt 'the buck stops'.
lines.known_text: And you said earlier that 'the buck stops'.

lines.speaker: Alun Davies
lines.target_text: Nad ydych chi'n teimlo fel bod gyda chi gyfrifoldeb i ystyried pethau'n bellach?
lines.known_text: Don't you feel that you have a responsibility to consider things further?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae yna wastad cyfrifoldeb ar gadeirydd neu aelod anweithredol o unrhyw gorff, wrth gwrs bod, ac mae hwnna yn barhaol o'r diwrnod cyntaf rŷch chi'n cael eich apwyntio hyd at ddiwedd eich cyfnod chi.
lines.known_text: There is always a responsibility on a chair or a non-executive member of any body, of course that's the case, and that is ongoing from the day of appointment up until the end of your period of service.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Fel dywedais i ar y cychwyn, mae mhwyslais i a fy niddordeb i trwy'r holl broses yma a heddiw o hyd ar les y staff.
lines.known_text: As I said at the outset, my emphasis and my interest through this whole process was and remains today on the well-being of the staff.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Does yna ddim gair wedi dod ataf i fod unrhyw aelod o staff presennol S4C yn meddwl y byddai fe o les i S4C pe bawn i yn ymddiswyddo heddiw.
lines.known_text: Not a word has been expressed to me that any member of the current S4C staff believes that it would be beneficial for S4C if I were to resign today.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Does dim un o'r cwmnïau cynhyrchu dwi wedi ymwneud â nhw neu wedi trafod gyda nhw yn ystod y cyfnod yma yn awgrymu y byddai fe'n llesol.
lines.known_text: Not one of the production companies that I've been involved with or have had discussions with during this period have suggested that it would be beneficial.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: I ddweud y gwir, mae'r neges yn glir iawn mai'r hyn maen nhw'n dymuno ei weld yn digwydd yw cyfnod o sefydlogi, a gadael i'r broses o wella sydd ar waith yn barod, fel gwnes i'n glir—.
lines.known_text: To be honest, the message is quite clear that what they want to see happening is a period of stability, allowing the process of improvement, which is already in play, as I made clear earlier—.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: O fewn S4C, mae'r awyrgylch gwaith wedi gwella'n sylweddol ers ymadawiad dau o'r prif swyddogion, a'r hyn sydd ei angen yw sefydlogrwydd i adael i'r broses hynny barhau i weithio.
lines.known_text: Within S4C, the working environment has improved significantly since the departure of two senior officials, and what we need now is stability to allow that process to continue to work.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Ocê, diolch am hynna.
lines.known_text: Okay, thank you for that.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Fe wnawn ni symud, yn olaf, at Tom.
lines.known_text: We'll move finally to Tom.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Ocê, fe wnawn ni fynd at Hefin a wedyn mynd at Tom.
lines.known_text: Okay, we'll go to Hefin and then Tom.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Hefin.
lines.known_text: Hefin.

lines.speaker: Hefin David
lines.known_text: Yes, just to observe that the conclusion the WRU took in these circumstances with regard to the chief executive and chair was exactly the opposite.

lines.speaker: Hefin David
lines.known_text: Can you see that that might be something that you would wish to consider?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Yr hyn ddywedwn i yw bod anawsterau o'r math yma mewn cynifer o sefydliadau a chyrff yng Nghymru wedi bod yn llawer rhy gyffredin yn ystod y cyfnod diweddar yma.
lines.known_text: What I would say is that difficulties of this kind in so many organisations and bodies in Wales have been too common during this recent period.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae undeb rygbi ond yn un o'r cyrff sydd wedi delio gyda phroblemau gwahanol.
lines.known_text: The rugby union is only one body that has dealt with different problems.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Yr hyn ddywedwn i yw bod yr amgylchiadau ym mhob achos yn wahanol, a bod yr ymatebion bob amser yn wahanol.
lines.known_text: What I would say is that the circumstances in every case are different, and that the responses have always been different.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Dydw i ddim yn gwybod digon am sefyllfa yr undeb rygbi i wybod digon amdano fe i allu mynegi barn.
lines.known_text: I don't know enough about the situation in the rugby union to know enough about it to be able to provide a view.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae'r hyn dwi wedi ei ddweud yn barod yn gosod allan fy marn i ynglŷn â S4C ac ynglŷn â'r hyn ddylai ddigwydd yn S4C, ac fy nghasgliad i ar hwnna yw fyddai i fi ymddiswyddo heddiw, neu ar unrhyw adeg arall cyn diwedd fy nhymor, ddim yn gwneud unrhyw les i S4C.
lines.known_text: What I've said already sets out my views with regards to S4C and what should happen in S4C, and my conclusion in that regard would be that for me to resign today, or at any other time before the end of my term, would not be of any benefit to S4C.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Gallaf ddychmygu y byddai fe'n gwneud i bobl eraill deimlo'n hapus ac yn hunanfodlon, ond, os siaradwch chi gyda'n staff ni neu gyda'n cyflenwyr, ein partneriaid ni, mae'r ymateb yn wahanol, ac mae rhai ohonyn nhw wedi mynegi hynny.
lines.known_text: I can imagine that it would make other people feel happy and self-satisfied, but, if you speak to our staff or with our providers, our partners, the response is different, and some of them have expressed that.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Roeddwn i'n gweld—.
lines.known_text: I see that—.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae yna lythyr gan un o'r cwmnïau cynhyrchu wedi dod at y pwyllgor yn mynegi'r farn yna.
lines.known_text: There's a letter from a production company that has been sent to the committee expressing that view.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Roedd cadeirydd cwmni annibynnol mwyaf llwyddiannus Cymru ar y radio bore yma yn mynegi'r un farn.
lines.known_text: The chair of one of the most successful independent television companies in Wales in a radio interview this morning expressed the same view.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Felly, o dan yr amgylchiadau hynny, dwi'n gwbl dawel fy meddwl fy mod i yn gwneud y peth iawn.
lines.known_text: Under those circumstances, I am completely at peace that I am doing the right thing.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Ocê.
lines.known_text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Fe wnawn ni symud at Tom.
lines.known_text: We'll move on to Tom.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Can I ask you what assessment you've made of staff absence and sickness levels during the tenure of the last chief executive?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Fel roedd Chris yn awgrymu yn gynt, doedd y wybodaeth oedd yn dod atom ni ddim yn ddigon cyson a manwl i'n galluogi ni i weld fod yna anhawster fan hyn.
lines.known_text: As Chris suggested earlier, the information provided to us wasn't sufficiently consistent and detailed to allow us to identify any difficulties here.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Rŷm ni wedi newid y drefn honno yn ystod cyfnod gwaith Capital Law, fel bod y dashfwrdd sydd nawr yn dod yn gyson—pedair gwaith y flwyddyn—at y pwyllgor pobl a thaliadau yn dangos hynny.
lines.known_text: We have changed that system during the period in which Capital Law undertook their work, so that the dashboard that is now provided regularly—four times a year—to the people and remuneration committee does identify those patterns.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: A beth mae e'n dangos yw, yn ystod y flwyddyn 2023, fe wnaeth bron i ddwywaith gymaint o bobl adael S4C ag oedd wedi gwneud yn y ddwy flynedd cyn hynny.
lines.known_text: And what it shows is that, during the year 2023, almost twice as many people left S4C than had done in the two years previous to that.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Felly, mae yna gamau wedi'u cymryd yn barod.
lines.known_text: So, steps have been taken already.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Fe fyddwn i'n derbyn yn llwyr fod angen gwella'r prosesau hynny.
lines.known_text: I would accept fully that we need to improve those processes.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Yn yr yn ffordd ag y mae dashfwrdd gyda ni sydd yn dangos faint o bobl sydd yn defnyddio Clic, a faint sydd yn defnyddio iPlayer, dylem ni hefyd fod yn derbyn hwnnw.
lines.known_text: Just as we have a dashboard that demonstrates how many people are using Clic, and how many people are using iPlayer, we should also be receiving that information.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: During this period of time, was that information available to you routinely?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Wel, ddim routinely. Fe ddaeth e i'r golwg. Oherwydd bod y broses yma wedi cymryd cyfnod hir o amser rhwng diwedd mis Ebrill a mis Tachwedd, mi oedd yna drafodaeth fewnol ynglŷn â'r materion yma yn digwydd, ac fe benderfynwyd bod angen gwella arno fe, a hefyd, wrth gwrs, fe gynhaliwyd arolwg staff yn ystod y cyfnod hwnnw, ac roedd yr arolwg staff yn dweud wrthym ni'r hyn a oedd yn mynd i ymddangos maes o law yn adroddiad Capital Law—sef bod yna lefel uchel iawn o anfodlonrwydd gyda'r arweinyddiaeth.
lines.known_text: Well, not routinely, no. It did emerge and because this process had taken a long period of time between the end of April and November, there was internal discussion on these issues that was ongoing, and a decision was taken that we needed to improve processes, and, of course, there was a staff survey conducted during that period, and that staff survey told us what would emerge in due time in the Capital Law report—that there was a high level of dissatisfaction with the leadership.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: So, just to help my understanding, there was no information that you were privy to that caused you any concern about staff sickness or staff absence prior to receipt of the letter in April 2023.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Nac oedd. Dim cyn derbyn llythyr BECTU.
lines.known_text: No, not until we received BECTU's letter.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ar ôl llythyr BECTU—
lines.known_text: Following BECTU's letter—

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: But before the letter, I understand that the staff sickness and absence levels were higher than normal.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae'n amrywio dros gyfnod o amser.
lines.known_text: It varies over a period of time.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: O ran absenoldeb o'r gwaith, fe oedd yna gynnydd yn ystod y cyfnod yma.
lines.known_text: In terms of absences from work, there was an increase during this period.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Hynny yw, gallaf i ddim, off top fy mhen, ddweud a oedd hwnna wedi dechrau yn 2023 cyn Ebrill, neu oedd e o Ebrill ymlaen.
lines.known_text: I can't, off the top of my head, say whether that had started in 2023, before April, or whether it was from April onwards.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: A dyna pam oedd rhaid gwneud yn siŵr bod gwell data gyda ni, a'i fod e'n dod aton ni yn fwy cyson.
lines.known_text: And that's why we had to make sure we had better data, and that we received it more regularly.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae'n rhywbeth sydd wedi bod yn destun trafodaeth yn y bwrdd, i sicrhau bod y matrix yna o fesuriadau o'r math yna ar gael, a'u bod nhw'n ar gael yn gyson.
lines.known_text: It's something that's been a topic of discussion in the board, to ensure that that matrix of measurements is available, and that they are available regularly.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Dwi'n credu taw dyna yw'r pwynt—mae'n rhaid eu cael nhw yn ddigon cyson i weld ydy'r newidiadau yn arwyddocaol.
lines.known_text: I think that is the point—you have to have them regularly enough to see whether the changes are significant.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ond, eto, doedd yna ddim byd cyn i lythyr BECTU gyrraedd a oedd yn gwneud inni feddwl bod yna rywbeth o'i le.
lines.known_text: But, again, there was nothing before BECTU's letter arrived that made us feel that there was something wrong.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Because I think it goes back to the point Alun was making, that even if that information wasn't regularly coming across your desk and you didn't see it, if you had a good temperature gauge, if you like, of the atmosphere in S4C during that period, that might have been something you might have proactively sought out.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: But I think the fact that that didn't happen suggests that you probably didn't have a good feel of what the temperature was like during that period of time.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Wel, doedd e ddim yn un digon da, yn sicr, achos pe bai e, fe fyddem ni wedi bod yn ymwybodol, 'Mae yna rywbeth o'i le fan hyn.'
lines.known_text: Well, it wasn't good enough, certainly, because if it was, we would have been aware that there was something wrong here.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ond doedd e ddim, a dyna pam fe'i newidiwyd e.
lines.known_text: But it wasn't, and that's why it has been changed.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae yna drefn newydd yn ei le nawr sydd yn rhoi'r wybodaeth honno.
lines.known_text: That's why there is a new process in place now that does provide that information.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: What I'm finding difficult to understand is we've got a report that is shocking, that says there was a toxic culture in the organisation for this period of time.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: You had staff absence levels that were going up, you had an initial letter from BECTU on which you were satisfied there was progress being made based on only one source.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: And my understanding was as well, as we've talked about earlier, that the churn of staff, if you like, the number of staff leaving during this period, was higher than average as well.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: But none of this prompted you to take any action up until that letter was received in April 2023.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: You're telling us that staff welfare was at the heart of all the decisions you've made, but that doesn't seem to apply to the period before the receipt of the second letter in April 2023.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Yr un peth y byddwn i yn ei ddweud yw nad dim ond gan un ffynhonnell roedden ni'n clywed bod yna welliannau ar waith, neu fod y cwynion a oedd wedi cael eu cyflwyno gan BECTU yn cael eu delio â nhw, a bod pethau yn gwella.
lines.known_text: The one thing that I would say is that we weren't hearing from one source only that improvements were happening, or that the complaints that had been presented by BECTU were being dealt with, and that things were improving.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Nid dim ond y prif weithredwr a oedd yn dweud hynny; mae yna gyfarwyddwr adnoddau dynol, mae yna aelodau eraill o'r tîm rheoli.
lines.known_text: It wasn't just the chief executive that was saying that, but there's an human resources director, and there are other members of the management team.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Felly, nid dim ond o un ffynhonnell oedd e'n dod.
lines.known_text: So, it wasn't just coming from one source.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ond fel dwi'n dweud, hynny yw, byddwn i wedi bod wrth fy modd pe baem ni wedi cael rhyw fath o early warning system a fyddai'n caniatáu inni ddweud, 'Mae eisiau i ni wneud mwy', ond doedd yna ddim.
lines.known_text: But as I say, I would have been delighted if we'd had some early warning system that would allow us to say, 'We need to do more', but there wasn't one.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Well, to build on that, staff, as we already mentioned, were leaving the organisation at an irregular level during this period of time.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Were staff surveys being undertaken?

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Were there exit interviews happening when staff left the organisation?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Na, dwi ddim yn credu oedd gan—.
lines.known_text: No, I don't think—.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Roedd yna nifer o wendidau, dwi'n credu, a ddaeth allan yn ystod ein trafodaethau, a ddaeth i'r golwg.
lines.known_text: There were a number of weaknesses, I think, that came out during our discussions.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Un oedd lefel isel iawn o asesu perfformiad staff.
lines.known_text: One was a very low level of performance assessment with staff.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Yn ystod y flwyddyn ddiwethaf, gwnaeth perfformiad aelodau'r tîm rheoli ddim cael ei asesu.
lines.known_text: During the last year, the performance of the management team wasn't assessed.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Gwnaeth dim un ohonyn nhw gael eu hasesu am dros flwyddyn.
lines.known_text: None of them was assessed for over a year.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: What I'm trying to—.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: You mentioned, 'I would have liked an early warning system', but it seems that one clear way that organisations get that warning system is by having those exit interviews, so that people—people in your position—when individuals leave an organisation, understand what the problems are.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: But that didn't seem to be happening at S4C.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Why wasn't that happening at S4C?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Wel, nid gyda chadeirydd nac aelod o'r bwrdd fyddai cyfweliadau yn digwydd wrth i bobl adael.
lines.known_text: Well, those interviews wouldn't happen with the chair or members of the board as people leave.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: No, I appreciate that.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: But if there is a problem, you would be aware of it, if the exit interviews are happening.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Because if the culture of fear was that current staff felt unable to come forward, then staff on their way out would probably have less qualms about doing it.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Na, dyw hwnna ddim yn wir, fel mae'n digwydd.
lines.known_text: Well, no. That's not the case, as it happens.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: I'm not saying that happens all the time, but it's far more likely that staff—

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Wel, digwyddodd e ddim yn yr achos yma, ac, eto, dwi'n adnabod yn bersonol rai aelodau o'r staff oedd wedi gadael yn ystod y cyfnod.
lines.known_text: Well, it didn't happen in this case, and, again, I know personally some of the staff members who did leave during that period.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Fe wnaethon nhw roi tystiolaeth i dîm Capital Law, ond gwnaethon nhw ddim mynegi'r amheuon hynny wrth iddyn nhw adael.
lines.known_text: They did provide evidence to the Capital Law team, but they did not express those concerns when leaving.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ac, wrth gwrs, un o'r pethau—. Ac eto, a gaf i eich cyfeirio chi yn ôl at yr adroddiad, fe welwch chi sylwadau gan y prif weithredwr am faint o bobl oedd hi'n dymuno gweld yn gadael y corff.
lines.known_text: And, of course, and, again, may I refer you back to the report, you will see comments from the chief executive on the number of people she wished to see leave the organisation.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Dwi'n credu bod e'n cael ei ddweud bod yna hanner cant o staff y byddem ni yn well off yn eu colli nhw.
lines.known_text: I think it said that there were 50 staff that we'd be better off without.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Felly, roedd yna ymdrech fwriadol, fan hyn, yn cael ei wneud i gael gwared ar aelodau staff. Nawr, doedd hynny ddim yn rhywbeth ddaeth i'm sylw i tan yr adroddiad ei hunan.
lines.known_text: So, there was a deliberate attempt here made to see staff leave and that wasn't something that came to my attention until the report itself was received.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ac a gaf i ddweud hefyd, wrth gwrs, mae cyfnod o newid—pan ŷch chi'n newid beth mae'r corff yn ei wneud, sut mae e'n gweithredu, mae e'n naturiol i newid staff, i ddod â gwaed newydd i mewn ac i weld rhai pobl yn gadael.
lines.known_text: And may I also say that, of course, any period of change—when you change how an organisation operates, then it's natural that there will be some churn in staff, that new blood will come in and that some staff will leave.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae hwnna—.
lines.known_text: There is nothing inherently wrong with that.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Does dim byd o'i le gyda hynny mewn egwyddor.
lines.known_text: But there is a way of doing that, and that's what all this is about, I think.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ond mae yna ffordd, a dyna beth mae hwn i gyd o gwmpas, dwi'n credu—y ffordd o wneud pethau.
lines.known_text: It's the way of doing things.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Digwydd bod, dwi'n eistedd ar fwrdd y Cyngor y Defnyddwyr Dŵr—yn ystod y tair blynedd diwethaf mae e wedi cael prif weithredwr newydd, sydd wedi arwain proses o newid mewnol, ond wedi gwneud hynny drwy fynd â'r staff gyda hi, drwy sicrhau bod perfformiad staff y Cyngor Defnyddwyr Dŵr, yn eu harolygon staff nhw, bron yn afresymol o uchel, oherwydd bod y ffocws wedi bod ar les, iechyd ac ar fod yn ofalus o staff.
lines.known_text: As it happens, I sit on the board of the Consumer Council for Water, and during the past three years, they've had a new chief executive, and they have led a process of internal change, but they've done so by taking the staff with them, by ensuring that the performance of the staff of the water consumer council, in their staff surveys, are almost irrationally high, because the focus has been entirely on the health, well-being and care of staff.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Nid dyna ddigwyddodd gyda ni.
lines.known_text: But that's not what happened with us.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Can I build on one point in terms of understanding the process around the termination and employment of staff.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: I understand you were responsible for the termination of the employment of the chief content officer, when that took place, and not the chief executive.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Listening to your answers yesterday to the Welsh Affairs Committee, you mentioned that the appointment of a new chief content officer would be made by the new chief executive.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: So, can you help me understand why the termination of the employment would be handled by the chair but the appointment would be handled by a chief executive?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Reit, oherwydd, yn syml iawn, yr amgylchiadau wnaeth arwain at ddiswyddo'r prif swyddog cynnwys, oedd ar ddydd Sadwrn yn Nantes, yn dilyn gêm rygbi.
lines.known_text: Because, quite simply, the circumstances that led to the dismissal of the chief content officer occurred on a Saturday in Nantes, following a rugby match.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Roedd y prif weithredwr yn bresennol yn yr un cyfarfodydd—nid cyfarfodydd yw'r gair iawn—yn yr un lleoliadau lle ddigwyddodd y digwyddiadau a arweiniodd at y penderfyniad.
lines.known_text: The chief executive had attended the same meetings—well, they weren't meetings—but the chief executive was present at the same locations where these events took place, which led to that decision.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Felly, roedd gan y prif weithredwr ddiddordeb yn y mater.
lines.known_text: So, the chief executive had an interest in that issue.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Doedd hi ddim wedi rhannu hynny gyda neb o fewn S4C, er bod y diwydiant yng Nghymru i gyd yn gwybod beth oedd wedi cael ei ddweud, wrth bwy yr oedd e wedi cael ei ddweud.
lines.known_text: She hadn't shared that with anyone within S4C, although the wider industry in Wales all knew what had been said and to whom.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Roedd e'n cael ei adrodd yn y wasg bron cyn i ni glywed amdano.
lines.known_text: It was being reported in the press almost before we'd heard about these events.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Felly, o dan yr amgylchiadau hynny, ac ar ôl derbyn cyngor ar broses a chyngor ar ddeddfwriaeth gyflogaeth a'r camau priodol i gymryd, fe gymerais i'r penderfyniad bod yn rhaid gweithredu'n syth er mwyn diogelu enw da S4C.
lines.known_text: So, under those circumstances, and having receiving advice on procedure and on employment law and the appropriate steps to be taken, I took the decision that action had to be taken immediately in order to safeguard the reputation of S4C.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Fel y cafodd ei gyfeirio ato'n gynt, dwi wedi bod yn y busnes yma am flynyddoedd lawer ac erioed wedi dod ar draws achos o uchel-swyddog yn ymddwyn yn y ffordd yna.
lines.known_text: As was mentioned earlier, I have been in this business for many years and have never come across a case of a senior official behaving in that way.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Pan fyddai'n dod, pe bai prif weithredwr newydd yn penderfynu bod angen—.
lines.known_text: If the new chief executive were to decide—.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Hynny yw, byddan nhw'n penodi rhywun, oni fyddan nhw, pe bai'n prif swyddog cynnwys fyddai fe neu gyfarwyddwr cynnwys, cyfarwyddwr rhaglenni—mae yna deitlau gwahanol.
lines.known_text: Of course, they will appoint somebody, whether that person will be a chief content officer or a director of content or a director of programming—there are all sorts of possible titles.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Pan fydd prif weithredwr newydd yn penodi, byddwn i'n disgwyl, fel mae'n digwydd, y byddai'r cadeirydd, pwy bynnag fyddai hwnna, yn cael ei wahodd i'r broses honno hefyd.
lines.known_text: When a new chief executive appoints, I would expect, as it happens, that the chair, whoever he or she may be, would be invited into that process.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Roeddwn i'n rhan o benodi Llinos Griffin-Williams i S4C, gan fod y swydd yn un o'r swyddi hynny sydd yn cario'r dyletswyddau ychwanegol o fod yn gyfarwyddwr gweithredol o'r bwrdd unedol cysgodol.
lines.known_text: I was involved in the process of appointing Llinos Griffin-Williams to S4C, because the post was one of those posts that carries the additional duties of being an executive director of the shadow unitary board.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: Could I just add on that point very briefly, Chair?

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.known_text: Very briefly, yes.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: I think the key point, as Rhodri has described, is the fact that this was an extremely unusual situation and there was a perceived need to act extremely quickly, which is why the chair, with external legal advice, set in place a process for those unique circumstances.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: So, it would not be the normal way that that would be handled.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: Indeed, I referred earlier to the fact that there was robust debate amongst directors, but that the non-executive directors were not able to be involved in that process because of the timescale.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: That was also something that was then discussed after the event, because that was very unusual.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: Had there been a way to have had a wider process, then that would clearly have been beneficial, but the view taken by the chair, with external specialist advice, was that the circumstances and the need to act so quickly justified taking that unusual process.

lines.speaker: Chris Jones
lines.known_text: But you're right, that's not how you would normally go about it.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Just very finally from me on the appointment of a new chief executive, you've mentioned that there's no real time frame on that appointment yet.

lines.speaker: Tom Giffard
lines.known_text: Is it your intention that that will happen in the remainder of your term?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.known_text: I think the board will be discussing that—

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Sori, pam dwi wedi troi i'r Saesneg, dwi ddim yn gwybod.
lines.known_text: Sorry, I don't know why I turned to English there.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Bydd y bwrdd yn trafod hynny pythefnos i heddiw.
lines.known_text: The board will discuss that a fortnight today.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: O ran pa mor bell y gallem ni fynd, fyddwn i ddim yn meddwl y byddai apwyntiad yn cael ei wneud, a bod yn berffaith onest, yn ystod gweddill fy nghyfnod i; fyddwn i ddim yn disgwyl y gallai ddigwydd o fewn y cyfnod hwnnw, ta beth.
lines.known_text: In terms of how far we could go, I wouldn't think that an appointment would be made, if I'm perfectly honest, during the remainder of my term of office; I wouldn't expect it to happen within that period.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Diolch.
lines.known_text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Dŷn ni'n ymwybodol iawn o faint o amser ychwanegol dŷch chi wedi aros gyda ni—diolch yn fawr iawn.
lines.known_text: We're very aware of how long you've stayed with us—thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Jest dau gwestiwn cryno iawn gen i, ar y diwedd.
lines.known_text: I have two very brief questions, at the end.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Roeddech chi wedi sôn wrth Alun, ac roedd e wedi'i godi ddoe, am y ffaith eich bod chi wedi gofyn am sawl cyfarfod gyda DCMS a bod hynny ddim wedi digwydd.
lines.known_text: You mentioned to Alun, and this was raised yesterday, that you'd asked for many meetings with DCMS and that that hadn't happened.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: A ydych chi'n meddwl ei fod e'n briodol, felly, taw'r Secretary of State sydd â'r pwerau yn y sefyllfa yma, os nad ydy'r Secretary of State yn dangos y diddordeb i eisiau cael cyfarfod?
lines.known_text: Do you think it's appropriate, therefore, that it's the Secretary of State who has the powers in this situation if the Secretary of State doesn't show an interest in having a meeting?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Dwi'n credu bod hwnna y tu hwnt i fy nyletswyddau i i fynegi barn ar bwy ddylai—.
lines.known_text: I think that's beyond my responsibilities in terms of expressing a view on who should—.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Hynny yw, dyna'r fframwaith rŷn ni'n gweithio ynddo fe—
lines.known_text: In other words, that's the framework that we're working within—

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Ond dydy'r fframwaith ddim, efallai, yn gweithio'n dda ar hyn o bryd, fel y mae.
lines.known_text: But perhaps the framework isn't working as well as it should at the moment.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Fel y dywedais i, rŷn ni wedi cwrdd yn achlysurol â rhai Gweinidogion o'r adran, ond fel y dywedais i, pan gynigiais i ein bod ni'n cyfarfod â'r Ysgrifennydd Gwladol i drafod y mater penodol yma, fel mae'n digwydd, gafodd y cynnig ddim ei dderbyn.
lines.known_text: As I said, we have occasionally met with some Ministers from the department, but as I said, when I proposed that we should meet the Secretary of State to discuss this specific issue, as it happens, that offer was not accepted.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae'n ymddangos i fi pan roedd y broses yn mynd yn ei blaen, doedd dim llawer o ddiddordeb, ond oherwydd y ffordd mae pethau wedi digwydd—a dyw'r ffordd hwnnw ddim y ffordd y byddwn i wedi dychmygu y byddai pethau wedi digwydd pan ddechreuodd y broses—mae gan bawb, bellach, ddiddordeb mewn pob un agwedd ar hwn.
lines.known_text: It appears to me that when this process was ongoing, there wasn't a great deal of interest shown in it, but because of the way things have panned out—and that isn't how I would have imagined things developing when this whole process started—everyone, now, is taking an interest in all aspects of this.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Mae hynny i'w ddisgwyl, onid yw e?
lines.known_text: That's to be expected, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Diolch.
lines.known_text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Jest y cwestiwn olaf: oes yna unrhyw beth dŷch chi'n difaru am yr holl sefyllfa?
lines.known_text: Just the final question: is there anything that you regret about the whole situation?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Oes.
lines.known_text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Dwi'n difaru y pwynt yma rŷn ni wedi bod yn ei drafod nad oedden ni fel bwrdd yn ymwybodol o'r pryderon yn gynt.
lines.known_text: I regret this point that we've been discussing that we as a board weren't aware of these concerns at an earlier stage.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Dwi yn difaru wrth edrych nôl fod y cylch gorchwyl wnaethon ni ei gytuno gyda Capital Law yn un oedd yn caniatáu i'r broses gymryd yn hir iawn.
lines.known_text: I do regret, with hindsight, that the remit that we agreed with Capital Law was one that allowed the process to take a long period of time.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Roedd yna resymau da.
lines.known_text: There were reasons for that.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Oherwydd y ffactor ofn yma dwi wedi cyfeirio ato fe, roedd hwnna'n rhan bwysig iawn o lunio'r cylch gorchwyl mewn termau eang iawn, oedd yn caniatáu, wrth gwrs, i bawb gyfrannu ato fe.
lines.known_text: Because of this fear factor that I have referred to, that was a very important part of drawing up the remit in very broad terms that, of course, then allowed everyone to contribute to this process.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Felly, mewn ffordd, fe greon ni broblem i ni'n hunain.
lines.known_text: So, in a way, we created a problem for ourselves.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Doedd cwyn BECTU ddim yn ymwneud â'r bwrdd, doedd e ddim yn ymwneud â llywodraethiant; roedd e'n ymwneud â'r tîm rheoli, fel roedd e wedi cael ei gyfeirio ato fe, er nad pob aelod o'r tîm rheoli oedd dan sylw, ond oherwydd bod dim modd bod yn benodol ynglŷn â chwynion, byddai fe ddim wedi bod yn briodol i enwi unigolion.
lines.known_text: The BECTU complaint didn't refer to the board or to governance; it related to the management team, as it was referred to, although not every member of that management team was involved, but they couldn't be specific about complaints, and it wouldn't have been appropriate to name individuals in that scenario.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Roedd BECTU wedi bod yn ofalus iawn yn hynny.
lines.known_text: BECTU had been very careful in that regard.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ond, wrth gwrs, fe wnaeth hynny olygu bod y broses yn un hirach a bod y broses yn caniatáu i bobl oedd, mewn gwirionedd, yn wrthrychau'r cwynion i fod yn cyfrannu ati hi.
lines.known_text: But, of course, that did mean that the process was lengthier and that the process did allow people who were the subjects of complaints to be contributing to it.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Dwi'n credu y byddai fe wedi bod yn fwy llesol, efallai, i'n staff ni ac iechyd meddwl ein staff ni trwy'r cyfnod yma, pe baem ni wedi cytuno ar gylch gorchwyl a oedd yn ffocysu, efallai, ar yr hyn oedd BECTU yn cwyno amdano fe, yn hytrach na dweud, 'Dewch aton ni i siarad am unrhyw beth ŷch chi'n moyn.'
lines.known_text: I do believe that it would have been more beneficial, perhaps, for our staff and for the mental health of our staff throughout this period, if we had agreed a remit that focused more on what BECTU were complaining about, rather than saying, 'Come to us to talk about anything that's on your mind.'

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ond gyda'r wybodaeth oedd gyda ni ar y pryd, roeddwn i'n ddigon hapus ar y pryd bod rhaid rhoi proses mewn lle oedd yn un agored iawn, er mwyn sicrhau bod gan bobl yr hyder i gyfrannu ati hi.
lines.known_text: But, with the information that we had at the time, I was quite content that we needed to put a process in place that was very open, in order to ensure that people had the confidence to contribute to it.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ond ydw i'n difaru hynny?
lines.known_text: But do I regret that now?

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Ydw.
lines.known_text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Diolch ichi.
lines.known_text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Rwy'n ddiolchgar iawn, dŷn ni i gyd yn ddiolchgar iawn, am yr amser ychwanegol dŷch chi wedi ei roi i ni y prynhawn yma.
lines.known_text: We're very grateful for the additional time you've provided this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Bydd transgript o'r hyn sydd wedi cael ei ddweud yn cael ei ddanfon atoch chi i chi nodi ei fod e yn gofnod teg o beth sydd wedi cael ei ddweud, ac efallai bydd ychydig o gwestiynau technegol doedden ni ddim wedi cael cyfle i fynd i mewn iddyn nhw y byddwn ni eisiau ysgrifennu atoch chi yn eu cylch.
lines.known_text: There will be a transcript of the meeting sent to you to ensure that it's a fair reflection of what's been said, and perhaps there will be some technical questions that we haven't been able to ask, and we'll want to write to you about those.

lines.speaker: Delyth Jewell
lines.target_text: Ond diolch yn fawr iawn ichi am fod gyda ni y prynhawn yma.
lines.known_text: But thank you very much for being with us this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi i gyd am eich amser a'r ffordd ŷch chi wedi mynd ati i'n holi ni.
lines.known_text: Thank you all very much for your time and for the way in which you have questioned us this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Dwi wedi dweud yn y pwyllgor yma o'r blaen ein bod ni yn gwerthfawrogi a bob amser yn barod i gael ein dal i gyfrif gennych chi fel Aelodau etholedig.
lines.known_text: I have said in this committee previously that do we appreciate and are always willing to be held to account by you as elected Members.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
lines.target_text: Er gwaethaf y ffaith bod yr amgylchiadau yn rhai amhleserus dros ben, dwi yn ddiolchgar iawn am y modd ŷch chi wedi holi'r cwestiynau yna i ni ac ymdrin â ni heddiw.
lines.known_text: Despite the fact that the circumstances are unpleasant, I am grateful for the way in which you have asked your questions and have dealt with us today.

lines.speaker: Rhodri Williams
